plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Does scale necessarily win? llama-2-13b vs llama-2-70b" (design-only; NO experiment has been run; the pure-Python scaffold is delivered and validated on synthetic tables only).

== 1. Pre-registered interpretation of "necessarily" ==
Two readings, with a fixed strength ordering. MAIN claim (statistical, across realistic regimes): for a comparison, define the standardized gap G = mean over fixed benchmarks of (score_70b − score_13b)/s, where s = 13B seed std on that benchmark (sign-flipped for lower-is-better metrics so positive always means 70B better). H0 "scale necessarily wins" is rejected for that comparison when meanG ≤ 0 AND the upper bound of the 95% percentile bootstrap CI ≤ 0. The PRIMARY test is at the adversarial cross-cell comparison (below); within-cell comparisons are reported for structure. SECONDARY claim (universal-flavored): every single benchmark/cell with raw Δ < 0 is reported as a per-benchmark inversion, explicitly subordinate to the statistical criterion — one inversion never decides the question by itself.

== 2. Design overview and identification ==
Decompose the 70B-vs-13B gap into: size effect (α), pre-training-adequacy effect (β·log(tok/param)), alignment effect (γ_base, γ_sft) and a size×PT-deficit interaction (δ), via a 2(size)×2(PT adequacy)×3(alignment) factorial with six cells: {adequate, insufficient} × {base, sft, rlhf}, each with a 13B and a 70B arm. Within-cell Δ_cell = 70B−13B (both trained under the same regime) isolates the pure size effect. The MAIN H1 test is the adversarial cross-cell comparison 70B@(insufficient, base) vs 13B@(adequate, rlhf) — the larger model trained worse than the smaller model trained well. Key identification: Llama-2 released base AND chat checkpoints at 13B/70B on the same 2T pre-training, so base-vs-chat within a size isolates alignment on identical weights and size comparisons hold pre-training fixed; only the insufficient-PT cells require actually training models.

== 3. Operationalization (flagged: source-adjacent facts vs design assumptions) ==
- Size: official Llama-2-13B/70B configs (tokenizer, 4096 context, 70B GQA). Fixed by task.
- Pre-training adequacy = tokens/parameter: Adequate = 2T (matches the Llama-2 recipe; =154 tok/param at 13B, ~28.6 at 70B) [ASSUMED source-adjacent fact, to verify against the primary source]; Insufficient = 500B for the 70B (~7.1 tok/param, deliberately well below the Chinchilla-optimal ~20 anchor) [DESIGN ASSUMPTION]; sensitivity cell at 1T separates absolute-token from tok/param effects.
- Alignment: base / SFT-only / SFT+two-stage RLHF (the Llama-2 recipe, ~27.5K human SFT examples, RM+PPO — ASSUMED, to verify). "Refined" = full recipe; "weak" = base or SFT-only.
- Controls held fixed: pre-training data distribution, optimizer/LR, context, tokenizer, harness/prompts, decoding.

== 4. Outcome suite (pre-registered) ==
Held-out perplexity (alignment-free PT probe; lower-is-better, reported separately from accuracy); MMLU 5-shot, HellaSwag 10-shot, WinoGrande 5-shot, ARC-c 25-shot (greedy); GSM8K 8-shot maj@100 (temp 0.7); HumanEval pass@1 with 200 samples (temp 0.8); MT-Bench-style + AlpacaEval-style win-rate vs a fixed reference (judge fixed across all cells). 8 eval seeds per cell for error bars.

== 5. Statistical analysis plan (implemented and sanity-tested in /workspace/design/analysis.py) ==
1. Per cell × benchmark: seed means per size, paired Δ, standardization by 13B seed std (fallback |mean13|), sign-flip for perplexity. 2. Bootstrap 95% CI (5000 resamples) on the aggregate G per cell and for the adversarial comparison. 3. Decision rule: negated = meanG≤0 AND CI_upper≤0 (main), plus a list of every benchmark with Δ<0 (secondary). 4. Linear model score ~ α·size70 + β·log(tok/param) + γ0·align_base + γ1·align_sft + δ·(size70 AND insufficient), fit per benchmark (or pooled on accuracy-scale benchmarks, perplexity excluded). 5. Derived negation boundary (an OUTPUT, not an assumption): tpp70* = tpp13_ref·exp(−α/β) (alignment-equal) and tpp70*(a) = tpp13_ref·exp(−(α+γ_a)/β) per alignment level, with bootstrap CI. Interpretation: tpp70* <~1 tok/param ⇒ PT deficiency alone cannot realistically negate size; 3–10 tok/param or a negative alignment-only gap (α + β·ln(28.6/154) + γ_a ≤ 0) ⇒ the moderator CAN negate size in trainable ranges. The δ interaction and per-benchmark heterogeneity are reported; the main decision is never based on δ alone.
Sanity-scaffold output (synthetic, NOT an experiment): H1-world test detected the adversarial inversion (meanG=−9.8, CI(−21.7, −3.1), negated, 7/7 benchmarks inverted) while the baseline adequate_rlhf cell stayed positive (CI(0.38, 1.89)); H0-world showed no negation and 0/7 inversions; regression signs matched the generative model (α>0, β>0, γ0,γ1<0) and the boundary came out tpp*=5.01 (H1) vs 0.01 tok/param (H0, effectively unreachable). These are scaffold-validation behaviors only.

== 6. Feasibility and execution tiers ==
Tier 0 (this workspace, DONE): stdlib-only analysis/statistics package + synthetic sanity tests (files below); no empirical claims. Tier 1 (primary, external GPU, cheap): evaluate released Llama-2 base/chat 13B/70B checkpoints — needs only evaluation (hundreds of A100-hours for sampling-based GSM8K/HumanEval) and gives the adequate cells and the alignment-negation evidence with zero pre-training. Tier 2 (heavy, external cluster): controlled pre-training of insufficient-PT cells. Cost estimates: ~6·N·D FLOPs ⇒ 70B@500B ≈ 2.1e23 FLOPs (≈0.4–0.5M A100-hours at ~40% MFU BF16), 70B@2T ≈ 8.4e23 (≈1.7M), 13B@2T ≈ 1.6e23 (≈0.3M), 13B@500B ≈ 4e22 (≈0.08M); full factorial ≈ 2.5M A100-hours/~285 A100-years — dominated by the 70B@2T arm that Tier 1 already supplies from released weights. DEGRADATION STRATEGY (adopted if the cluster budget is limited): pre-train only the insufficient arms, take adequate arms from released checkpoints, run a small-size pilot (1B/3B with the same 2×2×3 factorial, ~1–12k A100-hours) to validate the protocol and transfer β/γ, and optionally substitute a public partially-pre-trained 70B-scale checkpoint as an explicitly declared proxy. Nothing in this design is claimed to run in the CPU/offline workspace; only the analysis scripts run here.

== 7. Deliverables (in /workspace/design) ==
EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.md (full protocol), README.md (status + usage), analysis.py (pure-Python stats/scaffold), synthetic_data.py (H0/H1 synthetic generators), sanity_test.py (assertions, PASSED), synthetic_h0/h1.json, report_h0/h1.md, sanity_log.txt — every one explicitly marked as a NON-experiment validation scaffold.

context.question: Does increasing model size (as in comparing llama-2-70b to llama-2-13b) necessarily yield improved performance, or can insufficient pre-training and a lack of refined alignment negate the benefits of a larger parameter count?
